sector: Agricultural implements (Super Seeders, straw reapers, laser land levellers, rotavators)
headline: Revenue grew 63.1% in FY26 on a proforma basis with operating margin of 13.5%, but operating cash flow was 8.6% of PAT, three products carry 64.4% of sales, and the reference price of Rs 158.48 (28.1x EPS at the DRHP's own peer average) is about 38x on post-issue earnings.
red_flags: Proforma revenue Rs 2,074.5 m / 2,537.6 m / 4,139.7 m FY24-26 (+22.3%, +63.1%); restated FY24-25 exclude the businesses acquired from promoters (pp. 87, 91-92)
FY26 operating cash flow Rs 26.85 m = 8.6% of PAT; cumulative CFO/PAT 69.7%; inventory 132 days (pp. 88, 128)
Super Seeder, Straw Reaper and Laser Land Leveller = 64.40% of FY26 revenue; demand depends on CRM and SMAM subsidy schemes (pp. 56, 450)
Top customer 25.21%, top 10 50.04% of FY26 revenue; top 10 suppliers 40.53% of raw materials, no long-term contracts (pp. 33, 36)
ROE 53.89% and RoNW 44.26% pre-issue fall to about 8.8% on post-issue equity at the reference price; EPS Rs 5.64 becomes about Rs 4.21 (pp. 155, 158)
Two directors served while disqualified; adjudication pending. Promoters drew Rs 60.0 m remuneration in FY26 and hold Rs 55.0 m of company advances (pp. 94-95, 489)
reference_note: Rs 158.48 = DRHP industry-average P/E of 28.10x (VST Tillers 33.34x, Indo Farm 27.62x, Escorts Kubota 23.35x, closing prices 11-Sep-2026, p. 156) x restated FY26 basic EPS of Rs 5.64 (p. 154). It is a reference point built only from the DRHP, not a price band; the peers are tractor and tiller makers, not implements makers.

strengths: Proforma revenue +63.1% in FY26 to Rs 4,139.7 m on units sold of 19,111 (+56.2%) (pp. 92, 87, 158)
Current tax 29.3% of PBT in FY26, above the 25.17% statutory rate (p. 87)
Interest coverage 5.03x and debt/equity 1.89x FY26, from 2.70x and 50.36x in FY24 (p. 158)
Estimated 13% value share in straw reapers and 30% / 15% / 12% of subsidy-scheme Super Seeder units in MP / Haryana / Punjab, issuer-commissioned report (p. 446)
Capacity utilisation 76.3% FY26: 18,219 units on 23,875 installed (pp. 267-268)
weaknesses: Operating cash flow Rs 26.85 m vs PAT Rs 313.90 m in FY26 (p. 88)
Top three products 64.40% of revenue (p. 450); top customer 25.21% (p. 36)
Other expenses rose to 18.94% of revenue from 12.46% proforma FY25 (pp. 87, 92)
Inventory 132 days and receivable 45 days in FY26 vs payable 106 days (p. 128)
Working capital object of Rs 1,100 m is 36.7% of the fresh issue; modelled inventory days stay at about 130 (pp. 124, 128)
opportunities: Indian farm equipment market Rs 1,397 bn in FY26 to Rs 1,876 bn by FY30, 7.7% CAGR, issuer-commissioned estimate (p. 250)
Rs 716.64 m Dehlon expansion adds a fabrication unit, utilities unit and R&D unit; no orders placed yet (pp. 129-130)
Presence in 20 states in FY26 vs 15 in FY25 and 10 in FY24 (p. 158)
Briquette and pellet machinery for crop residue conversion (p. 446)
threats: CRM and SMAM subsidy changes could cut demand for flagship products (p. 56)
Monsoon and rural-income cycles; fragmented holdings, 86% of operational holdings are small and marginal (CARE report, p. 241 of PDF)
Expansion site is 16.20 acres leased from a promoter at Rs 0.08 m per month (p. 129)
Erstwhile related parties still buy and sell with the company: Rs 164.91 m purchases and Rs 70.00 m sales FY26 (p. 94)
FY26 is the first consolidated year; no history of the combined business as a listed entity (pp. 301-302)

flags: AMBER: DCF and relative diverge by -46.6% - the divergence is the finding; name its cause
AMBER: TV above 75% of EV - DCF is mostly a terminal guess
model.reverse_dcf: Current free cash flow is negative: no multiple can be stated, and the entire price rests on a turn that has not yet begun.
